questions.question: Who is the author of the essay 'School’s Goodbye'?
questions.explanation: The essay is written by Lord Eustace Percy.

questions.question: What was the former profession of Lord Eustace Percy?
questions.explanation: Lord Eustace Percy was a former Minister of Education in Britain.

questions.question: To whom is the message in 'School’s Goodbye' primarily addressed?
questions.explanation: The text is a message to school children about to leave school.

questions.question: What does the author desire to send the students before they leave?
questions.explanation: The text says, 'before you go we desire to send you our best wishes for your future welfare'.

questions.question: According to the author, when does education finish?
questions.explanation: The author hopes students will not 'think that your education is finished' and states you must continue it to succeed.

questions.question: What is required to 'secure' success in life?
questions.explanation: Success 'only comes to those who work hard and continue learning'.

questions.question: How should a student choose a trade or profession?
questions.explanation: The author advises: 'Choose with the greatest care'.

questions.question: What type of occupation should students 'avoid as far as you can'?
questions.explanation: The text says to 'avoid as far as you can any occupation that leads nowhere'.

questions.question: One should aim at work that has in it the promise of what?
questions.explanation: Students should 'Aim rather at work that has in it the promise of an interesting and happy future'.

questions.question: Who should a student ask for advice if they are in doubt about their choice of profession?
questions.explanation: The author says, 'do not hesitate to ask advice from one of your teachers'.

questions.question: Success in life depends largely on ________.
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Success in life depends largely on good health'.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT mentioned as a way to keep the body fit?
questions.explanation: The text lists 'cleanliness, fresh air, regular habits, and suitable recreations'.

questions.question: What is the consequence of smoking in youth, according to the author?

options.B: It stunts the body and clouds the brain.

questions.explanation: The author warns, 'Smoking in your youth stunts the body, and clouds the brain'.

questions.question: How is 'drink' (alcohol) described in the essay?

options.C: The deadly enemy of health and efficiency

questions.explanation: The text states, 'beware of drink. It is the deadly enemy of health and efficiency'.

questions.question: What is described as a 'priceless possession'?
questions.explanation: The author reminds students, 'your character is a priceless possession'.

questions.question: Character should be kept ________.
questions.explanation: The author says, 'Keep it therefore untarnished'.

questions.question: How should a student behave toward their rivals?
questions.explanation: The text advises students to be 'fair to your rivals'.

questions.question: To whom should students be 'kind and helpful'?

options.B: All who are weak and suffering

questions.explanation: The text says to be 'kind and helpful to all who are weak and suffering'.

questions.question: Why should gambling be avoided in every form?

options.B: It is a 'mean game' trying to get something for nothing.
options.D: It is only for old people.

questions.explanation: The author calls gambling a 'mean game trying to get something for nothing and at somebody’s cost'.

questions.question: What should students make 'provision' for?
questions.explanation: The text says: 'Make provision for hard times'.

questions.question: What should be avoided in leisure hours?
questions.explanation: The author says, 'In your leisure hours, avoid mere idling'.

questions.question: What should fill a student's leisure hours?
questions.explanation: Leisure hours should be filled with 'interesting hobbies, good books, and with companionships... for good'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'To a large extent, you will be known by the ________ you keep.'
questions.explanation: The text states, 'you will be known by the company you keep'.

questions.question: A student will be a credit to their family with a sound mind in a ________.
questions.explanation: The concluding paragraph mentions 'With a sound mind in a sound body'.

questions.question: What quality refers to 'polite or well-mannered' behavior?
questions.explanation: The glossary/matching exercise identifies 'courteous' as 'polite or well-mannered'.

questions.question: What does the word 'untarnished' mean in the context of character?

options.B: Pure and bright (without any black spot)

questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'untarnish' as 'free from / without any black spot'.

questions.question: What does 'stunt' mean in 'stunts the body'?
questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'stunt' as 'to prevent something or somebody from growing properly'.

questions.question: The term 'sap' in the text means to ________.
questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'sap' as 'gradually weaken'.

questions.question: What does 'above all' mean in the text?
questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'above all' as 'most importantly'.

questions.question: What word means 'the health and happiness of people'?
questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'welfare' as 'the health and happiness of people'.

questions.question: Which conjunction can be used to join two contrasting statements like 'He is leaving school' and 'He will not forget his school days'?
questions.explanation: The language section demonstrates using 'although' to join contrasting statements.

questions.question: In imperative sentences like 'Avoid gambling', the subject is usually ________.
questions.explanation: In imperative sentences 'the subject ‘you’ is usually not expressed'.

questions.question: What is the imperative form of 'I want you to get up early in the morning'?

options.B: Get up early in the morning.

questions.explanation: Imperative sentences omit the subject and express the command directly.

questions.question: What is the '-ing' form of 'begin'?
questions.explanation: The verb 'begin' doubles the 'n' in the '-ing' form: beginning.

questions.question: The author says leaving school is like saying goodbye to your own ________.
questions.explanation: The lead-in says 'it is like saying goodbye to your own family'.

questions.question: What 'clouds the brain' according to the text?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'Smoking... clouds the brain'.

questions.question: What should students have the courage to stand up for?

options.B: What is good, pure and noble

questions.explanation: The author encourages students to 'have courage to stand up for what is good, pure and noble'.

questions.question: A good citizen should be loyal to the ________ of their nation.
questions.explanation: The author mentions 'loyalty to the duties of your nation'.

questions.question: What word in the text means 'be on your guard against something'?
questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'beware of' as 'be careful, be on your guard against something'.

questions.question: What 'exercise over you an influence for good' in your leisure hours?
questions.explanation: The author suggests associations 'calculated to exercise over you an influence for good'.

questions.question: Success is not easily ________.
questions.explanation: The line is 'Success in life is not easily secured'.

questions.question: What is 'deadly enemy' to efficiency?
questions.explanation: Alcohol/drink is called 'the deadly enemy of health and efficiency'.

questions.question: What must you do to succeed in any trade or profession?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'if you are ambitious to succeed... you must continue your education'.

questions.question: The author advises students to be ________ to everybody.
questions.explanation: The author advises being 'truthful in all things, considerate to everybody'.

questions.question: What word means 'actively seeking success, wealth, or status'?
questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'ambitious' as 'actively seeking success, wealth, status etc.'.

questions.question: The author urges students to be truthful in ________ things.
questions.explanation: The text says 'Be truthful in all things'.

questions.question: Which of these contributes to a 'credit to your family'?
questions.explanation: The final paragraph links good character and manners to being a credit to the family.

questions.question: What is the noun form of 'profess'?
questions.explanation: The grammar exercises require converting 'profess' into its noun 'profession'.

questions.question: What happens when you say goodbye to school?

options.B: You move to a wider world.

questions.explanation: The text states 'You move out from school to the wider world'.

questions.question: Which of the following is 'suitable recreation'?

options.B: A hobby or pastime for health

questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'recreation' as 'a hobby, amusement, game or pastime'.

questions.question: Lord Eustace Percy gives advice on how to become good human beings and ________.
questions.explanation: The text mentions telling students how to become good 'human beings and citizens in future'.

questions.question: What is the '-ing' form of 'gamble'?
questions.explanation: The verb 'gamble' drops the 'e' and adds '-ing': gambling.

questions.question: Which phrase means 'permanently'?
questions.explanation: The matching exercise defines 'for good' as 'permanently'.

questions.question: How should one be in 'all things' according to the text?
questions.explanation: The author says, 'Be temperate in all things'.

questions.question: The author hopes students will not 'think that your ________ is finished'.
questions.explanation: The text states: 'hope you will not... think that your education is finished'.

questions.question: Where was Lord Eustace Percy a Minister of Education?
questions.explanation: He was a 'former Minister of Education in Britain'.

questions.question: What word matches 'unselfish, giving thought to the happiness of others'?
questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'considerate' as 'unselfish, giving thought to the happiness and comfort of others'.

questions.question: A sound mind exists in a sound ________.
questions.explanation: The text concludes with the phrase 'With a sound mind in a sound body'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Avoid anything that will ________ your health.'
questions.explanation: The author warns students to 'Avoid anything that will sap your health'.

questions.question: What is the noun form of 'educate'?
questions.explanation: The exercise on converting verbs to nouns uses 'educate' to 'education'.

questions.question: Which of these is a duty of a good citizen mentioned in the exercises?
questions.explanation: The exercises list 'Sacrifice for the nation' as a duty of a good citizen.

questions.question: What quality does character give to an individual, making it 'priceless'?
questions.explanation: The author calls character a 'priceless possession'.

questions.question: Complete the phrase: 'Success in life is not easily ________.'
questions.explanation: The line from the text is: 'Success in life is not easily secured'.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'courteous'?
questions.explanation: The matching exercise defines 'courteous' as 'polite or well-mannered'.

questions.question: How should students treat the weak and suffering?
questions.explanation: The text says to be 'kind and helpful to all who are weak and suffering'.

questions.question: A student should seek advice from their ________ if in doubt.
questions.explanation: The text advises to 'not hesitate to ask advice from one of your teachers'.

questions.question: What is the opposite of 'belief' as shown in other chapters but relevant to 'although' grammar?
questions.explanation: The prefix exercise in Chapter 4 shows disbelief = dis + belief.

questions.question: The author says students move out to a ________ world.
questions.explanation: The text mentions moving to the 'wider world'.

questions.question: What word means 'to make uncertain or confused'?
questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'cloud' as 'to make uncertain or confused'.

questions.question: What is the final wish of the author for the students?
questions.explanation: The essay ends by saying with character and loyalty, they will be 'a real success'.
